key_notes.12.4833333: The hand swings the face back round toward us: one fast frame, as in the film.
key_notes.11.9: Still side-on; the hand holds it there. Hold.
key_notes.12.4: Anticipation of the turn back: the hand moves down onto the face's left edge, face still narrow.
key_notes.13.4: The hand has left the frame at the left; the clock alone, facing us.
key_notes.12.9: The hand draws back to the left, the arm shortening; breakdown so the withdrawal is continuous.
key_notes.13.2333333: The hand reaches the left edge; the clock holds.
key_notes.10.9: Mid turn away, fastest change: face half as wide, bells sliding together over the drum.
key_notes.13.4833333: End: the clock stands alone; the hand is kept just outside the frame so it does not blink out.
key_notes.11.2333333: The turn away arrives: face edge-on at the left, the drum's side toward us. Extreme.
key_notes.12.9833333: The hand keeps pulling back to the left; the clock holds.
key_notes.11.5666667: Held side-on, face a sliver, leaning a little under the hand. Extreme held.
key_notes.10.65: The hand starts to turn the clock: the face narrows and the side begins to show. Start of the turn away.
key_notes.12.7333333: Contact released: the hand lets go and starts to slide back; the clock stands on its own, settled.
key_notes.10.4: The hand has hold of the clock's top; the clock faces us. Start pose.
key_notes.12.5666667: THE LINE: the clock faces us again, one round face, the hand pressed to its left side.
key_notes.12.2333333: The face starts to come back: first widening. End of the hold.
